Title: Diagnosis

Details: The failing test `testCOMPRESS335` loads a TAR archive named "COMPRESS-335.tar" to verify TAR input stream handling. The current bug report states that this TAR file has a checksum field with zero padding on the left rather than the expected NULL-SPACE terminator padding on the right, causing the checksum to be interpreted incorrectly as invalid.

The TAR checksum validation is handled by the method `TarUtils.verifyCheckSum(byte[] header)`. This method parses the checksum field starting at offset `CHKSUM_OFFSET` (148) and spanning `CHKSUMLEN` (8) bytes in the TAR header. The implementation parses digits only up to 6 octal digits, and skips trailing bytes by setting them to spaces for the sum calculation. It treats the checksum as valid if either the unsigned or signed byte sum matches the parsed stored checksum.

According to the Javadoc, TAR checksum values are typically stored as six-digit octal numbers followed by a NUL and a space character. However, some TAR implementations may use different padding formats (like zero padding to the left). The implementation's current strict parsing of only the first 6 octal digits from the fixed offset and reliance on trailing characters being spaces or nulls causes it to lose the final two digits of the checksum when zero padding is left aligned.

Therefore, the root cause of the failure is that `TarUtils.verifyCheckSum` assumes checksum is right-padded (NULL-SPACE terminator) and only considers the first 6 octal digits, ignoring the possibility of left zero padding. This causes the last two digits in the zero-padded checksum to be ignored, causing a mismatch and the checksum validation to fail erroneously for such TAR files.

Recent bug reports about different archiver input streams or entry naming are unrelated to the checksum validation logic or this particular failure.

This diagnosis explains why the test fails on the "COMPRESS-335.tar" archive and matches the current bug report. The faulty assumption in `TarUtils.verifyCheckSum` about checksum padding and digit extraction is the likely cause.

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
